study.title: Electroacupuncture at HT5 + GB20 promotes brain remodeling and significantly improves swallowing function in patients with stroke
study.blinding: single-blind; outcome assessors blinded; patients and acupuncturists not blinded
study.population: stroke patients with dysphagia recruited by the Department of Rehabilitation Medicine of Panyu District Central Hospital from May 2022 to June 2023
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) patients with stroke diagnosed according to the updated definition for the 21st century (Sacco et al., 2013) and diagnosed with subcortical stroke by computed tomography (CT) or magnetic resonance imaging (MRI); (2) patients with dysphagia confirmed by videofluoroscopic swallowing study (VFSS); (3) patients with stable vital signs, with a duration of the disease of 1 to 12 months, and aged between 30 and 85 years old; and (4) patients with the ability to give informed consent
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) dysphagia due to neurologic conditions other than stroke; (2) patients with severe cognitive impairment or inability to cooperate with treatment; (3) patients with recurrent stroke (not first-time stroke); and (4) patients with a history of sedation or other medications that affect cortical excitability

arms.dropouts: 1 patient declined to participate in the secondary assessment

interventions.procedure_label_exact: electroacupuncture at HT5 + GB20 combined with conventional swallowing rehabilitation
interventions.anatomical_location_exact: GB20: neck, below the occipital bone, between the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles; HT5: palmar side of the forearm, at the radial edge of the ulnar flexor carpi radialis tendon
interventions.needle_size_exact: GB20: 1.5 cun milli-needle; HT5: 1 cun milli-needle
interventions.penetration_exact: GB20: oblique insertion; HT5: direct insertion
interventions.depth_exact: GB20: 1 cun toward the throat; HT5: 0.5 cun
interventions.manipulation_exact: flat tonic and flat diarrhea method; after obtaining Qi, electroacupuncture device connected
interventions.electrical_intensity_exact: 0.2 to 0.6 mA, tolerated by the patients
interventions.treatment_period_exact: once a day, 6 times a week, for two weeks
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: same acupuncturist, at least 5 years of acupuncture experience
interventions.participant_instructions_exact: patient was seated in the upright position
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: based on awakening the mind and dispelling the wind, opening the orifice, and facilitating the pharynx; combined with the principle of 'taking acupoints from the near part' and 'where the meridians pass, the main treatment reaches'

interventions.treatment_period_exact: six times a week for two weeks
interventions.practitioner_description_exact: same physiotherapist performed traditional dysphagia treatments
interventions.treatment_rationale_given_exact: traditional dysphagia treatments such as sensory stimulation, tongue retraction exercises, and oropharyngeal muscle strengthening exercises

neuroimaging_methods.scanner_manufacturer_model_exact: NirSmart-6000A (Danyang Huichuang Medical Equipment Co., Ltd., China)
neuroimaging_methods.sequence_exact: functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS); two wavelengths: 730 nm and 850 nm
neuroimaging_methods.scan_duration_exact: 150 s total (10 s baseline + 4 cycles of 35 s each [15 s task + 20 s rest])
neuroimaging_methods.analysis_software_exact: NirSpark software package (HuiChuang, China); SPSS 22.0 (SPSS Inc., Chicago, IL, USA)
neuroimaging_methods.normalization_template_exact: Montreal Neurological Institute standard brain template in NirSpace using a spatial registration technique (Danyang Huichuang Medical Equipment Co., Ltd., China)
neuroimaging_methods.motion_exclusion_exact: spline interpolation applied to correct motion artifacts in each channel; expert removed low-quality signals
neuroimaging_methods.filtering_exact: band-pass filtered between 0.01 and 0.2 Hz to remove physiological noise
primary_neuroimaging_metrics: functional connectivity (FC) via Pearson correlation with Fisher's r-to-z transform

extraction_notes.note: No formal deqi measurement instrument (e.g., MASS, SACS, Southampton Needle Sensation Questionnaire) was used or reported. Deqi is mentioned only as a procedural criterion ('after obtaining Qi') with no quantitative sensory data.
Expectancy and credibility were not formally assessed. No expectancy questionnaire, credibility scale, or blinding index was administered to participants.

No sham acupuncture control was used. The authors note: 'Due to the characteristics of patients with post-stroke dysphagia and electroacupuncture, it was not feasible to implement sham electroacupuncture in this study.' This limits interpretation of specific acupuncture effects.

The neuroimaging modality is fNIRS (not fMRI or EEG). No MNI coordinates are reported for individual channels or ROIs; results are summarized at the regional level (e.g., LPM, RPM, RM1, RS1, LM1). No coordinate table exists in the paper.
No multiple comparison correction was reported for any neuroimaging analysis. This is a potential limitation for interpreting the significance of multiple ROI comparisons.
Change scores (delta values) between pre and post for clinical outcomes are not explicitly reported in the tables; only pre and post mean ± SD values are given with within-group p-values.

The fNIRS channel layout and probe positions are described conceptually and shown in Figure 1A but individual channel MNI coordinates are not tabulated in the main paper. The spatial registration to MNI space is stated but no coordinate table is provided.

Table 3 presents functional connectivity values described as 'Mean ± SD' but the units and scale are not explicitly stated as Fisher's z-values in the table header. The text clarifies Fisher's r-to-z transformation was used, so values are interpreted as z-values.

The Table 1 baseline comparison for RM1~LM1 shows p = 0.0060, which is statistically significant at the 0.05 level. This baseline difference between groups for RM1~LM1 functional connectivity may affect interpretation of post-treatment between-group comparisons for this edge.
Supplementary Table 1 referenced for baseline demographic and clinical characteristics is not included in the provided PDF pages. Full demographic data not fully extractable.
The paper does not report individual participant data, effect sizes (Cohen's d, etc.), confidence intervals, or adjusted p-values for any comparison.

The n_analyzed for between-group neuroimaging comparisons is inferred as 48 total (24 per group) based on participant flow diagram. The paper does not explicitly state the n for each between-group imaging comparison.

The fNIRS instrument used (NirSmart-6000A) is a near-infrared spectroscopy device, not an fMRI scanner. The field_strength_tesla field is therefore not applicable and set to null. The modality is classified as 'other' with description in sequence_exact.
